note: Assertions for the PRE-4.0.0 core surface — the one maxio-sdk documents. Everything else in this directory describes generator 4.0.0, and on a pre-4.0.0 fixture ~100 of those fail by construction; that delta is baselined in maxio-pre-4.0.0-drift.txt so the job goes red when it CHANGES. This file is the other half, and it is the half that was missing: the positive claims maxio's own dotnet-* skills make had no executable backing at all, so they could rot exactly the way the 4.0.0 claims did before this tool existed. Each one below is verified against asadali214/advanced-billing-sample-sdk@v1.0.2; the three marked `run-verified` were settled by executing the SDK, not by reading it. These carry `surfaces` so they do not run against the 4.0.0 fixtures, where they would be false.

assertions.claim: The pre-4.0.0 core surface is 88 Core/*.cs files — against 122 on 4.0.0. The count is the cheapest surface discriminator there is.
assertions.defends: the core-surface stamp at the top of every maxio-sdk dotnet-* skill

assertions.claim: The transport arm is a bare .Handle<HttpRequestException>() sitting directly beside the result arm, with no method test of its own — so a transport fault is retried on EVERY verb, POST included.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience § Notes; maxio-sdk:dotnet-testing § Notes — 'is retried on every verb, POST included'

assertions.claim: HttpMethodsToRetry is consulted INSIDE the result arm, not above both arms — so it gates status retries only. This is the exact inverse of the 4.0.0 claim that the method filter gates both arms, and copying that claim here would be a falsehood about which writes get resent.

The verb the status arm filters on is read off response.RequestMessage — so a test stub that leaves RequestMessage null makes status retries silently never fire, and a 503-then-200 test 'proves' a policy that is not running.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-testing — 'Do not drop the response.RequestMessage = request line from the stub'

assertions.claim: MaxRetries is handed to Polly's MaxRetryAttempts unguarded. run-verified: MaxRetries = 0 therefore throws a Polly ValidationException when the CLIENT IS CONSTRUCTED — the floor is 1, and there is no way to turn retries off through this knob.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience § Retries — 'MaxRetries = 0 throws in Polly (the floor is 1)'

assertions.claim: There is no `if (options.MaxRetries > 0)` guard around the retry strategy — the 4.0.0 escape hatch that makes 0 mean 'no retries' does not exist here.

A retry-ineligible request runs on ResiliencePipeline.Empty — it loses the retry strategy AND the per-attempt timeout with it, leaving HttpClient.Timeout as the only bound. On 4.0.0 the same request keeps a timeout-only pipeline.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience § Bounding a call — 'requests the pipeline declares retry-ineligible, which run with no per-attempt timeout at all'

assertions.claim: CanRetry is a property of the BODY, not the verb: a binary request cannot be replayed and so opts out, while a JSON request — including a JSON POST — is eligible and does go through the full pipeline.
Nothing clamps the computed delay — there is no MaxDelay ceiling on this surface, so a large BackOffFactor grows unbounded. 4.0.0 clamps at 60s.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience — 'there is no Retry-After handling and no delay clamp'

assertions.claim: RetryOptions declares no MaxDelay property at all, so the clamp is absent from the option surface as well as from the factory.

There is no RetryOptions.Disabled() on this surface. Combined with Polly's floor of 1, retries cannot be switched off through RetryOptions at all — the only way out is a request the pipeline declares ineligible.
Jitter is a whole-millisecond Random.Next draw over MaxJitter, not the NextDouble() * MaxJitter of 4.0.0 — and MaxJitter <= zero short-circuits to no jitter rather than throwing.

RawClient wraps the send in no try/catch whatsoever, so NOTHING is translated on the way out. run-verified: options.Retry.Timeout therefore surfaces as Polly.Timeout.TimeoutRejectedException (InnerException: TaskCanceledException) and is NOT a TaskCanceledException — a boundary guard written as `when (ex is HttpRequestException or TaskCanceledException)` does not match it. 4.0.0 catches and rethrows, which is why the same guard is correct in the paypal-sdk and twilio-sdk copies and wrong here.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-error-handling § Connection failures; maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience § Bounding a call

assertions.claim: The timeout strategy is added AFTER the retry strategy, making it inner — so options.Retry.Timeout bounds one attempt, not the call. Only a CancellationToken bounds the whole call.
assertions.defends: maxio-sdk:dotnet-configuration-resilience § Bounding a call — the three-layer table
